newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- NOV 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- NOV 12.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI

--By late last night it was still not clear when and under what terms the Athens Stock Exchange would resume trading. The government, through National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou, is pushing for the soonest possible resumption of trading, fearing the diffusion of the crisis, while brokers insist that the ASE remain shut until all debts to the depository are cleared. Brokers fear a premature resumption of trading would allow those firms involved in the scandal to cover their backs.
--The continuation of uncertainty on the bourse hides dangers for mutual funds, with concern being expressed that the crisis of confidence will lead to a mass sell off of shares.

--The government has announced a range of new state titles to cover the state's increased lending needs of one trillion drachmas.Three new investment products will be offered: a five-year fixed return bond with an interest rate of around 10 percent, a two-year final return bond, and a bond pegged to cost of living, to be issued next year.

--Today's inner cabinet meeting is expected to take the final decision on the 1997 budget and economic spending. The inclusion of the defence and education ministers, as well as the ruling party PASOK's secretary, indicates that the meeting will be the first time the government's economic choices gets the widest possible approval.
--Citibank increases interest rates on short-term loans and business credit.
--The Ionian Bank's general director is expected to leve his position within the next few days.
IMERISIA

--Procedures to straighten out the situation on the bourse will take at least two-three days, in which the ASE will not operate, sources say. However, some members, primarily banks, believe the clean-up operation can continue while trading resumes.
--A three-member committee of brokers will be established at the depository today to assist in the inspection of all transactions on the ASE.

--1997 will see interest rates on fall two percentage points: the finance ministry's fiscal adjustment programme includes new products as well as institutional changes to the management of the public debt.
--Moody's may upgrade the long- and short-term foreign currency deposit ratings of seven Greek banks.
KERDOS
--The battle of conflicting interests puts the brake on the market as brokers and government divide into opposing camps. The delayed clearance of transactions cannot be justified.
--Debtors to the state will be able to resettle with favourable terms, according to a new amendment to be tables in Parliament.
--Only new state titles will be taxed, sources say.
EXPRESS

--New taxation measures will be discussed at today's inner cabinet meeting and tomorrow's cabinet as well as by PASOK party bodies this coming week. Cabinet will look at the bills for spending cutbacks and the abolition of tax exemptions while PASOK will consider the direction of economic policy.
NAFTEMBORIKI
--The government refuses to cover the 'black hole' at the stock exchange and the Athens Stock Exchange goes it alone. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
